saints.name: St. Gregory the Great
saints.title: Pope and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The Roman prefect turned monk who as pope styled himself "servant of the servants of God" and shepherded the Church through a broken age…
biography: Born of a Roman senatorial family about 540, Gregory rose to be prefect of the city before giving away his wealth, founding monasteries, and becoming a monk. Drawn from the cloister to serve as papal envoy and then, in 590, elected pope, he governed Rome amid plague, famine, and the Lombard invasions with tireless charity and administrative genius.

He sent St. Augustine of Canterbury to convert the English, reformed the Church's worship and chant (which bears his name), and wrote enduringly on pastoral care and Scripture. One of the four great Latin Doctors, he is honoured as "the Great."
saints.knownFor: The mission to the English and his reform of the Church's liturgy and pastoral life.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), "Pope St. Gregory I (the Great)"
